metadata.title: Teachers’ pathways to the profession and their attitudes toward diverse classrooms

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TALIS 2018 teacher questionnaire data from 48 countries/economies, with a two-stage stratified sampling design (schools selected first, then teachers within selected schools). For the United States, the authors report a main survey of 220 schools with 20 teachers per school and an analytic set of 2,554 responses from 2,560 invited teachers. The manuscript does not report the use of TALIS sampling weights or any specific weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) and does not mention replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so weight application cannot be confirmed. Analytically, the authors restrict the TALIS teacher questionnaire to 19 items used to build four constructs (TIP, TCT, TPD, TCC) and handle missingness using FIML rather than listwise deletion.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variables are latent constructs derived from TALIS teacher questionnaire items (TIP, TCT, TPD, TCC) estimated via confirmatory factor analysis/latent variable modeling, not cognitive achievement scores with TALIS/PISA-style plausible values. The paper states that missing data were handled using full information maximum likelihood (FIML), which is treated here as a multiple-imputation-like approach in the schema mapping. Plausible values handling is therefore not applicable because the analysis does not involve PV-based achievement outcomes.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used TALIS 2018 teacher questionnaire data for the United States, restricted to lower secondary teachers (grades 7–9). The authors drew 52 questions from the teacher questionnaires but retained only 19 TALIS items to create four constructs (TIP, TCT, TPD, TCC) for the analysis. The analytic sample includes 2,554 teacher responses out of 2,560 invited teachers; missing responses on the selected variables were handled with full information maximum likelihood (FIML).

main_findings.dataset_used: TALIS 2018 United States (lower secondary teachers, grades 7–9)
main_findings.target_variable: Teachers’ Importance for Profession (TIP) latent construct
main_findings.performance_metrics: Measurement model fit (four-factor CFA): χ²(59)=224.58, CFI=.974, TLI=.966, RMSEA=.033 [90% CI .029–.038], SRMR=.028. Measurement invariance across FCT vs SCT: ΔCFI=.001 (weak) and ΔCFI=.003 (strong), both supporting invariance. Latent regression on gender: β=0.251 (p=.000) for FCT group; β=0.332 (p=.000) for SCT group. Additional analysis (Teachers’ Training for Culturally Diverse Teaching (TCT) latent construct): Measurement model fit (four-factor CFA): χ²(59)=224.58, CFI=.974, TLI=.966, RMSEA=.033 [90% CI .029–.038], SRMR=.028. Measurement invariance across FCT vs SCT: ΔCFI=.001 (weak) and ΔCFI=.003 (strong), supporting invariance. Latent regression on gender: β=0.187 (p=.004) for FCT group; β=0.243 (p=.001) for SCT group. Additional analysis (Teachers’ Practices for Diversity Implementation (TPD) latent construct): Measurement model fit (four-factor CFA): χ²(59)=224.58, CFI=.974, TLI=.966, RMSEA=.033 [90% CI .029–.038], SRMR=.028. Latent regression on gender: β=-0.245 (p=.001) for FCT group; β=-0.282 (p=.000) for SCT group. Additional analysis (Teachers’ Class Composition (TCC) latent construct): Latent regression on gender: β=-0.155 (p=.055) for FCT group; β=-0.132 (p=.119) for SCT group. Measurement model fit (four-factor CFA): χ²(59)=224.58, CFI=.974, TLI=.966, RMSEA=.033 [90% CI .029–.038], SRMR=.028.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TALIS 2018 United States data for lower secondary teachers (grades 7–9), the study leveraged teacher career choice (FCT vs SCT) and teacher gender to model the latent Teachers’ Importance for Profession (TIP) construct, finding that female teachers rated TIP higher than male teachers in both FCT and SCT groups (β=0.251 and β=0.332, both p<.001). This indicates that recruitment and professional support strategies may need to account for gender-linked differences in how teachers value job stability and social equity when preparing teachers for diverse classrooms, while noting the study is based on self-report latent constructs rather than causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses TALIS 2018 teacher questionnaire data for the United States, focusing on lower secondary teachers (grades 7–9). The authors build four latent constructs—TIP (importance/attitudes), TCT (training/coping for culturally diverse teaching), TPD (diversity implementation practices), and TCC (class composition)—from 19 selected TALIS items and estimate a four-factor CFA model with strong fit (χ²(59)=224.58, CFI=.974, TLI=.966, RMSEA=.033, SRMR=.028). Missing data were handled with full information maximum likelihood (FIML). Measurement invariance across first-career teachers (FCT) vs second-career teachers (SCT) was supported (ΔCFI=.001 for weak and ΔCFI=.003 for strong). The study reports gender-linked differences in TIP and TCT (female higher) and TPD (male higher), while TCC shows no significant gender effect; however, the analysis is based on self-reported perceptions and does not involve ML prediction or PV-based achievement outcomes.
